title: Korean Life Apps
summary: The app layer of daily life in Korea: Naver Map for places, Baemin for food delivery, Kakao T for taxis, identity verification for Korean services, and Papago/Naver Dictionary for checking Korean fast.

units.title: Use Naver Map for Directions and Places
units.situation: You need to find a cafe, hospital, station exit, bus route, or walking direction in a Korean map app.
units.goal: I can search a Korean place name, ask for the address, check a route, and show a saved location to a driver or staff member.

keyPhrases.en: I will look it up on Naver Map.
keyPhrases.note: 지도 = map. -에서 marks the app or place where the action happens.

keyPhrases.en: Please send me the address.
keyPhrases.note: 주소 is safer than only a building name, especially for taxis and delivery.

keyPhrases.en: Which exit is this?
keyPhrases.note: Subway exits matter in Korea. The same station can have many exits.

keyPhrases.en: How long does it take on foot?
keyPhrases.note: 걸어서 = by walking. 얼마나 걸려요? asks duration.

keyPhrases.en: Please take me to this address.
keyPhrases.note: Show the Korean address on your phone if pronunciation is hard.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Please send me the address here.

dialogue.speaker: Friend
dialogue.en: I will send a Naver Map link.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.ko: 고마워요. 몇 번 출구로 가면 돼요?
dialogue.romanization: gomawoyo. myeot beon chulguro gamyeon dwaeyo?
dialogue.en: Thanks. Which exit should I go to?

beginnerGuide.title: Search in Korean first
beginnerGuide.body: Korean place names often work better in Hangul than in English. If you only know the English name, copy the Korean name from the business card, website, or chat message.

beginnerGuide.title: Save the address line
beginnerGuide.body: For taxis, deliveries, clinics, and appointments, keep the Korean address and building name ready. A screenshot can be faster than trying to pronounce it.

beginnerGuide.title: Check exit and floor
beginnerGuide.body: Many places are near a specific subway exit or inside a building. Look for 출구 (exit), 층 (floor), and 호 (unit number).

checkpoints: I can ask someone to send a Korean address or map link.
I can ask which subway exit to use.
I can show a saved address to a taxi driver or staff member.
I know that Korean names usually search better than English names.
steps: Copy or type the Korean place name into Naver Map.
Check the subway exit, bus stop, walking time, and building floor.
Save or screenshot the Korean address before you leave.
If you take a taxi, show the address and say 이 주소로 가 주세요.
If you get lost, ask 여기가 어디예요? and show the map screen.

deepLinks.label: Naver Map
deepLinks.note: Map, place search, public transit, walking, and driving directions.

units.costs: Using the map is free. Data charges depend on your mobile plan.
units.notes: KakaoMap and Google Maps can also help, but Naver Map often has stronger Korean local search and place details.

units.title: Order Food on Baemin
units.situation: You want food delivered to your home, office, dorm, or hotel and need to read common order and delivery words.
units.goal: I can find a menu item, check delivery fee and minimum order, write a delivery memo, and respond if the rider calls.

keyPhrases.en: I will order through Baemin.
keyPhrases.note: 배민 is the common short name for 배달의민족.

keyPhrases.en: Please leave it at the door.
keyPhrases.note: A common delivery memo for contactless drop-off.

keyPhrases.en: Please leave out disposable spoons and chopsticks.
keyPhrases.note: Useful if you do not need utensils.

keyPhrases.en: The address is correct.
keyPhrases.note: Say this if the rider calls to confirm.

keyPhrases.en: How long will delivery take?
keyPhrases.note: 얼마나 걸려요? asks duration.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.ko: 네, 맞아요. 문 앞에 놔 주세요.
dialogue.romanization: ne, majayo. mun ape nwa juseyo.
dialogue.en: Yes, that is right. Please leave it at the door.

beginnerGuide.title: Read the four money lines
beginnerGuide.body: Before ordering, check 배달비 (delivery fee), 최소주문금액 (minimum order), 예상 시간 (estimated time), and 결제금액 (total payment).

beginnerGuide.title: Delivery memo matters
beginnerGuide.body: Use 요청사항 or 배달 요청사항 for notes like 문 앞에 놔 주세요. Keep it short and polite.

beginnerGuide.title: Be ready for a phone call
beginnerGuide.body: Riders may call if the entrance, gate code, or address is unclear. Practice 주소가 맞아요, 문 앞에 놔 주세요, and 잠시만요.

checkpoints: I can recognize delivery fee, minimum order, estimated time, and total payment.
I can write a simple delivery memo.
I can confirm my address if the rider calls.
I can request no disposable utensils.
steps: Set your delivery address in Korean and check the building name.
Pick the restaurant and menu, then check 배달비 and 최소주문금액.
Add options and coupons before payment.
Write a short delivery memo if needed.
Keep your phone nearby until the food arrives.
units.costs: Delivery fee, small-order fee, and menu prices vary by restaurant, distance, time, and promotion.
units.notes: If you do not have a Korean card or phone verification yet, delivery apps may be limited. In that case, ask a friend or order directly by phone from places that accept it.

units.title: Call a Taxi with Kakao T
units.situation: You need a taxi late at night, with luggage, in the rain, or when the subway route is hard.
units.goal: I can set pickup and destination, confirm the fare range, message the driver, and say the destination politely.

keyPhrases.en: I will call a Kakao taxi.
keyPhrases.note: 부르다 = to call, often used for taxis.

keyPhrases.en: Please come here.
keyPhrases.note: Useful if pickup location is slightly confusing.

keyPhrases.en: Please go to this address.
keyPhrases.note: Show the app screen or Korean address.

keyPhrases.en: Please open the trunk.
keyPhrases.note: Useful with luggage.

keyPhrases.en: I will pay by card.
keyPhrases.note: 카드로 = by card.

beginnerGuide.title: Set pickup carefully
beginnerGuide.body: Pickup location is the common failure point. Check the side of the road, building entrance, and nearby landmark before calling.

beginnerGuide.title: Show the address, not your pronunciation
beginnerGuide.body: If the destination name is hard, show the Korean address and say 이 주소로 가 주세요.

beginnerGuide.title: Fare is not always final
beginnerGuide.body: Taxi apps can show estimated fare, but traffic, route, tolls, late-night surcharge, or taxi type can change the final amount.

checkpoints: I can say I will call a taxi.
I can ask the driver to come here or go to this address.
I can ask for the trunk to be opened.
I know the estimated fare may change.
steps: Set pickup and destination before calling.
Check the taxi type and estimated fare.
Stay near the pickup point and watch the car number.
If the driver calls, say 여기로 와 주세요 or 잠시만요.
When you get in, show the destination and say 이 주소로 가 주세요.
units.costs: Taxi fare depends on distance, time, route, taxi type, traffic, and possible surcharges.
units.notes: If you feel unsafe or the destination is wrong, ask to stop in a clear public place and call 112 for immediate danger.

units.title: Sign Up, Verify Yourself, and Use Korean Services
units.situation: A Korean app asks for 회원가입, 로그인, 본인 인증, phone verification, card registration, or a public-service login.
units.goal: I can recognize the login and verification steps, ask for help, and know when a Korean phone number or ARC may be required.

keyPhrases.en: Do I need to sign up?
keyPhrases.note: 회원가입 = first-time account creation.

keyPhrases.en: I cannot log in.
keyPhrases.note: 안 돼요 = it does not work / I cannot.

keyPhrases.en: How do I verify my identity?
keyPhrases.note: 본인 인증 is a frequent gate in Korean apps.

keyPhrases.en: The verification code is not coming.
keyPhrases.note: 인증번호 = verification code.

keyPhrases.en: Do I need an Alien Registration Card?
keyPhrases.note: Some services require a Korean identity record or phone plan tied to your name.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: How do I verify my identity?

dialogue.speaker: Staff
dialogue.en: You can verify with your mobile phone number.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: The verification code is not coming.

beginnerGuide.title: 회원가입 and 로그인 are different
beginnerGuide.body: 회원가입 is creating the account for the first time. 로그인 is entering an account you already made.

beginnerGuide.title: Name matching matters
beginnerGuide.body: Korean verification often checks whether your name, birthdate, phone number, and ID record match. If your phone plan is not in your name, verification may fail.

beginnerGuide.title: Public services need extra patience
beginnerGuide.body: Government, bank, and telecom services may require ARC information, certificates, or phone verification. Do not assume a social login is enough.

checkpoints: I can tell 회원가입 from 로그인.
I can ask how to complete identity verification.
I can explain that the verification code is not arriving.
I know some Korean services may require an ARC or Korean phone number in my name.
steps: Check whether the screen says 회원가입 or 로그인.
Keep your passport name, ARC name, and phone-plan name consistent when possible.
If a code does not arrive, check the phone number and spam-blocking settings.
For government services, start from the official site rather than a random search result.
Ask a staff member: 본인 인증 어떻게 해요?

deepLinks.label: GOV.KR for foreigners
deepLinks.note: Official Korean government service portal for foreigners.

units.costs: Most sign-up and verification steps are free. Phone plans, certificates, banking, or document issuance can have separate fees.
units.notes: Never share verification codes with strangers. If someone asks for an 인증번호 outside the app flow, treat it as suspicious.

units.title: Use Papago and Naver Dictionary Without Getting Misled
units.situation: You need to understand a sign, menu, text message, app screen, or grammar explanation quickly.
units.goal: I can translate for rough meaning, check key words in a dictionary, and ask a native speaker a better follow-up question.

keyPhrases.en: What does this mean?
keyPhrases.note: The fastest question when showing a word, sign, or screenshot.

keyPhrases.en: Does this expression sound natural?
keyPhrases.note: Ask this after machine translation, because meaning and naturalness are different.

keyPhrases.en: How do you say it in easier words?
keyPhrases.note: Good when a dictionary answer is too formal.

keyPhrases.en: How would you say it on KakaoTalk?
keyPhrases.note: Register check: spoken chat can be very different from textbook Korean.

keyPhrases.en: I will take a photo and translate it.
keyPhrases.note: Useful for signs, menus, and notices.

dialogue.speaker: Native
dialogue.en: The meaning is right, but it is a little stiff.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.en: Then how would you say it on KakaoTalk?

beginnerGuide.title: Translate for meaning, not final wording
beginnerGuide.body: Machine translation is useful for rough meaning, but it may sound stiff, too formal, or too direct. Always check naturalness for messages you will send.

beginnerGuide.title: Dictionary before guessing
beginnerGuide.body: If one word controls the whole sentence, check that word in a dictionary. Menus, forms, and notices often turn on one key noun or verb.

beginnerGuide.title: Ask better native questions
beginnerGuide.body: Instead of asking 'Is this right?', ask 이 표현 자연스러워요?, 더 쉬운 말로 어떻게 말해요?, or 카톡으로는 어떻게 말해요?

checkpoints: I can ask what a word or expression means.
I can check whether a translated expression sounds natural.
I can ask for a simpler or more KakaoTalk-like version.
I know not to send machine translation blindly in sensitive messages.
steps: Use Papago or a camera translation feature for rough meaning.
Pick the words that seem important and check them in a dictionary.
If you will send the sentence, ask a native whether it sounds natural.
Ask for a shorter KakaoTalk version when the result sounds too formal.
Save useful corrected sentences into your review deck.

deepLinks.label: Naver Papago
deepLinks.note: Translation helper for text and images.

units.costs: Basic translation and dictionary lookup are free online. Data charges depend on your mobile plan.
units.notes: For medical, legal, immigration, or money issues, use translation as a helper, not as the final authority.
